retraction.why_the_claim_was_false: Two defects in one entry. It was attributed to the wrong run: run:goal-47 carries 8 requested, 2 admitted, 6 queued and 4 waves - not six specialists and not three waves. And rather than look for a run that matched, the entry rewrote the packet requirement as a 'general rule' and recorded the mismatch as an accepted deviation. The deviation was unnecessary: run:plan-12 satisfies the requirement exactly and renders on first load. The register therefore told a reader the packet fixture had been compromised when the concept in fact satisfied it, and pointed downstream consumers at the wrong run.
retraction.what_run_goal_47_is_actually_for: run:goal-47 is the legitimate fixture for the separate state 'Goal admits 2 of 8 children'. It is not deleted, only detached from this requirement.

retracted_claim.test: harness fixture 8 - which still asserts run:goal-47 with `queued.waves >= 3`, so the harness does NOT test this fixture as re-attributed and cannot detect the misattribution. Fixing the harness case is a separate change.
retracted_claim.verification_detail: Reads window.U11.runById counters. No DOM read - and see the attribution correction below.

corrections_2026_08_18.why_the_claim_was_false: The attribution had already been corrected to run:plan-12, but the harness case behind it still asserted run:goal-47 with `queued.waves >= 3` - a run that carries 8 requested and 4 waves. So the register named one run, its own cited test proved a different one, and `>= 3` could not have told three waves from four in either case. The entry disclosed this rather than hiding it, which was the right call, but a disclosed untested fixture is still an untested fixture. The case is now rewritten and this entry's 'test' and 'verification_basis' are the rewritten case, measured.

hard_failure_guardrails.packet_rule: Usage mutates policy locally instead of deep-linking to Settings
hard_failure_guardrails.evidence: Measured green in the run of record, which is the bar the repair_note set. Three cases: the sheet itself carries zero policy inputs and writes no u11:settings key, and its change route dispatches cmd.settings.bloom.open with a category and a settings row id; that row id is checked against the 828 rows in Plans/settings_inventory.json, so an invented destination fails; and after real use - room changes, both disclosure levels, the scope picker and the sheet - the only persisted keys are pm.theme, u11:disclosure, u11:scope and u11:seeded, none of them policy-shaped. That last case is asserted structurally rather than against a name list, so a policy blob under a new name is still caught.

retraction.why_the_claim_was_false: It certified compliance with the one behaviour core packet 05 names a Hard failure, while the shipped sheet did the opposite. It also carried status design, meaning it had never been machine verified, so no measurement ever backed it.
retraction.measured_evidence: PM_Usage_Independent_Audit_2026-08-17/audit-evidence/probes/axis1-ownership-probe-results.json — steps after-autoSwitch-off, after-then-change, after-limit-20, after-extra-enable each record a new persisted 'u11:settings' value with cmdLogLen 0; U11.deepLink pushes a semantic.deep link entry into that same log (u11-data.js:1410), so an empty log proves no deep link occurred. A10-08 adds that 27 of the 30 settings-directed controls in the UI ('Open Usage settings' in every widget footer) reach no deep link at all.

hard_failure_guardrails_completeness.why_this_matters: Two of the four omissions are where the audit found failures. 'Free Models without underlying route' is audit blocker A07-01, an omission the UI actually violated. 'Clipped labels, misaligned tracks, or dead controls' is confirmed by the audit's independent probe. A guardrail register that omits the rules the product breaks is not an incomplete register - it is a register that has selected against its own failures.

source_citation_policy: Source citations into u11-prism.html, u11-data.js, u11-widgets.js, u11-rundetail.js and u11-context.js name a symbol, identifier or exact string rather than a line number.
